Why cheaper

Why are we cheaper?

A website is expensive mostly because of the time spent on it. I have cut that time, not the care. Here is how, and what you keep.

Optimisation

A little band of automations for the repetitive work, and no middleman to pay.

Everything checked by hand

I proofread, test on a phone and put it online myself.

A price on display

€500 for the website, the same for everyone, with no quote to wait for.

Nothing sacrificed

Quality, security, visibility on Google and a real person to talk to are all still there.

What you really pay for in a website

A website is mostly time. When a freelancer builds it entirely by hand, they spend days on it, sometimes weeks: the mock-up, the layout of each screen, the first drafts of the text, the settings, the tests. That time has a price, and it is what makes up the bill.

According to public benchmarks gathered in France, a 15-page showcase website with SEO, made by a freelancer, usually costs between €2,000 and €3,000. Looking after it often costs between €60 and €200 a month. These prices are not inflated: they reflect the work involved.

My idea is different. I spend less time on what repeats from one website to the next, so that small businesses and associations can also have a professional website, at a price they can afford.

No magic: just optimisation

Alongside the websites I build myself, I spent time programming a little band of companions. They are my automations, which I drew as little monsters. Each of them takes care of one repetitive but useful task, working independently. Add direct access to French hosting providers, and you have the whole secret behind these prices. There is nothing magic about it, just optimisation.

A little band for the repetitive work

Many steps come up again on every project, then every month once the website is live. The band takes care of them, and I always check what it has done. Work that used to take me days is now done in a few hours.

  • While building it: Bricou, the builder, puts together a first layout, and Plume, the writer, prepares a base for the texts. Then I rework everything in your own words.
  • After going live: Pistache, the guardian, takes care of backups, the safety copies of your website, and of maintenance, meaning the technical checks that keep it in working order. Cerise, the secretary, welcomes your requests.
  • For you: nothing to learn, nothing to keep an eye on. I handle everything, and you have no effort to make.

The result: a single page is ready in 3 to 5 days, and a site with several pages in 1 to 2 weeks.

Direct hosting

Your website is hosted in France: it is kept on machines that run day and night, with hosting providers I deal with directly. There is no middleman between them and me, and that is also what keeps the monthly plans at a low price.

What I do by hand

The little monsters are quick, but they decide nothing. I design and build your website: I listen to you, I make the choices and I rework everything they prepare.

  • Proofreading: every page, every text, every opening time and every price shown.
  • Phone testing: I go through the website on several devices, just as your customers will.
  • Checking: the links, the form, the loading speed, the information meant for Google.
  • Going live: I connect your domain name, the address of your website, I install the padlock that protects your visitors and I publish the website myself.
  • Your changes: each one passes before my eyes before it is published, even when Bricou prepared it.

Your website only goes live after it has been through my hands.

A price on display, no quote needed

With many providers, you have to ask for a quote, wait, then compare. Here, the price is written on the website and it is the same for everyone: €500 for the website, up to 15 pages. The pages you do not use work for Google. When you order, there is just one option, paid once: the online shop at €200. The SEO Pack, at €25, is added later from your client area: 10 more pages to be found on Google (this is what is called SEO).

You pay 25% when you order and the balance on delivery, all at once or in 6 or 12 interest-free instalments. After that, the choice is yours. A monthly plan keeps the website alive, with no commitment: Peace of Mind at €10 or Growth at €20. Or website only: I hand over the website’s code, and you install it yourself. The full details are on the prices page.

Market prices, honestly

Compared with the same 15-page website made by a freelancer, the gap is often 4 to 5 times.

The difference then lies in what comes with it: checking by hand, follow-up after the launch, and someone who answers when you have a question.

These ranges are rough guides, taken from public pages in November 2026. Each provider sets their own prices, and a particular project may cost more or less.

What is not sacrificed

A lower price does not mean rushed work. Here is what you keep, whichever website you choose:

  • Quality: a modern, clear and fast website, designed for phones first.
  • Security: the padlock in the address bar, maintenance, backups, and a website watched over day and night.
  • Visibility: the SEO basics are set up on every page, so that Google understands your business.
  • A real person to talk to: when you write, I am the one who answers, within 72 hours.
  • Your freedom: the domain name is in your name, and the plan stops whenever you decide.

And if your project goes beyond what I do well, like a custom-built app or a catalogue of thousands of products, I will tell you from our very first conversation.

Your questions

Does cheaper mean worse?

No. The price is lower because I spend less time on what repeats, not because I skip steps. Every website is proofread, tested on a phone and checked before it goes live.

Is my website made automatically?

No. I design and build your website myself. My little band only takes care of what repeats: a basic layout, early drafts of the text, some settings. After that, I go back over everything by hand, make the choices with you and put the website online myself.

Are there any costs on top of the price shown?

No. The website costs €500, then the plan costs €10 or €20 a month if you let me put it online. The online shop and the SEO Pack are optional, and their prices are shown on the website.

Why is there no quote?

Because most websites for the self-employed, tradespeople, shops or associations are built in the same way. A fixed price is simpler for you and for me. For an unusual project, I will tell you so honestly.
